q-wikinger-nordeuropa-23#question: Which Viking leader was baptized after his defeat at Edington in 878?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-23#explanation: Guthrum was baptized, withdrew to East Anglia and ruled there as king.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-24#question: What were the tributes called with which English kings induced Viking armies to leave?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-24#explanation: Large sums of silver were paid as Danegeld, especially under King Æthelred from 991.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-25#question: According to tradition, who was the first permanent settler of Iceland?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-25#explanation: According to the Book of Settlements, Ingólfr Arnarson made his home around 874 on the site of present-day Reykjavík.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-26#question: On which plain in southwestern Iceland did the Althing meet?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-26#explanation: Þingvellir lies east of Reykjavík and is today a national park and UNESCO World Heritage Site.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-27#question: How did Iceland adopt Christianity around the year 1000?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-27#choices.1: Through a decision of the Althing
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-27#choices.2: Through a crusade called by the pope
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-27#choices.3: Through the baptism of the Icelandic king
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-27#explanation: The lawspeaker Þorgeir declared that all Icelanders should become Christians in order to avoid a civil war.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-28#question: Which Frankish monk preached in Birka in Sweden around 830?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-28#explanation: Ansgar, later archbishop of Hamburg-Bremen, is venerated as the “Apostle of the North”.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-29#question: Which Norwegian king fell at Stiklestad in 1030 and was afterwards venerated as a saint?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-29#explanation: Olaf Haraldsson became, as Saint Olaf, “Norway’s eternal king” and the country’s patron saint.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-30#question: In which city was Saint Olaf buried, which became Norway’s most important place of pilgrimage?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-30#explanation: Nidaros Cathedral was built over Olaf’s tomb and drew pilgrims from all over northern Europe.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-31#question: Which Norwegian king drowned around 1000 in the naval battle of Svolder?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-31#explanation: According to tradition Olaf Tryggvason leapt overboard when his ship the “Long Serpent” was captured.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-32#question: Whom did Cnut the Great marry in 1017 to consolidate his rule in England?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-32#explanation: Emma was the widow of King Æthelred; their son was Harthacnut.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-33#question: In which force did Harald Hardrada serve before he became king of Norway?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-33#choices.0: In the Byzantine emperor’s Varangian Guard
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-33#choices.1: In the army of William of Normandy
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-33#choices.2: In the crusader army before Jerusalem
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-33#choices.3: In the bodyguard of the caliph of Córdoba
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-33#explanation: Harald fought for Byzantium as a Varangian, in Sicily among other places, and returned with great wealth.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-34#question: Which English king defeated the Norwegians at Stamford Bridge in 1066 but lost shortly afterwards at Hastings?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-34#explanation: After his victory in the north Harold Godwinson hurried south and fell at Hastings on 14 October 1066.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-35#question: Which trading place on the Schlei was one of the most important markets of the Viking Age?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-35#explanation: Hedeby linked North Sea and Baltic trade; its remains lie near Schleswig.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-36#question: What is the name of the rampart that protected Denmark in the south against the Frankish Empire?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-36#explanation: The Danevirke was extended several times, among others around 808 under King Godfred.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-37#question: Where did much of the silver in Viking Age hoards on Gotland come from?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-37#choices.3: From India via the Red Sea
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-37#explanation: Tens of thousands of Arab dirhams reached the North via the rivers of eastern Europe.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-38#question: What are the Old Norse narratives called that were written down in Iceland about families of the settlement period?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-38#explanation: The sagas of Icelanders were composed mainly in the 13th and 14th centuries from oral tradition.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-39#question: Which Danish king conquered the trading town of Visby on Gotland in 1361?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-39#explanation: The conquest of Visby helped drive the Hanseatic towns into an alliance against Valdemar IV.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-40#question: Which peace ended the war between the Hanseatic League and Denmark in 1370?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-40#explanation: In the Peace of Stralsund the Hanseatic League gained trading privileges and the castles of Scania for 15 years.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-41#question: Who was crowned joint king of the three Nordic realms at Kalmar in 1397?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-41#explanation: Eric of Pomerania, Margaret I’s great-nephew, was king of the union; real power lay with Margaret until 1412.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-42#question: Which island submitted to the Norwegian king between 1262 and 1264?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-42#explanation: In the Old Covenant the Icelanders recognized King Haakon IV; the Icelandic Commonwealth came to an end.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-43#question: Which method showed in 2021 that wood was felled at L’Anse aux Meadows in the year 1021?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-43#choices.1: Traces of a solar storm in the tree rings
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-43#explanation: A known solar storm of 993 left a carbon-14 spike in the tree rings, which made it possible to date the felling precisely to 1021.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-44#question: What do the Vinland sagas call the native people whom the Norse met in America?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-44#explanation: The sagas call them Skrælings; conflicts with them contributed to the abandonment of the settlement attempts.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-45#question: Which lawspeaker announced the adoption of Christianity at the Althing around 1000?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-45#explanation: Þorgeir, himself still a pagan, decided after a day and a night of reflection that all Iceland should become Christian.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-46#question: Which city became the seat of the first archbishopric for all Scandinavia in 1103 or 1104?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-46#explanation: Lund in Scania then belonged to Denmark; Nidaros and Uppsala received their own archbishoprics only in 1152/53 and 1164.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-47#question: Which Arab envoy described Rus traders and a ship burial on the Volga in 922?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-47#explanation: Ibn Fadlan travelled to the Volga Bulgars on behalf of the caliph and left one of the rare eyewitness accounts of the Rus.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-48#question: Which chronicler described Rollo’s agreement with Charles the Simple about a hundred years later?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-48#explanation: No text of a treaty of 911 survives; the detailed account comes from Dudo of Saint-Quentin.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-49#question: Which Obodrite trading place did the Danish king Godfred destroy in 808?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-49#explanation: Godfred brought the merchants from Reric into his kingdom, probably to Hedeby.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-50#question: What is the name of Snorri Sturluson’s history of the Norwegian kings?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-50#explanation: Heimskringla was written around 1230 and tells the story from the legendary beginnings to 1177.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-51#question: Which territory did Valdemar IV sell to the Teutonic Order in 1346 in order to win back Denmark?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-51#explanation: With the proceeds Valdemar redeemed pledged parts of Denmark.
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-52#question: In which year did the Kalmar Union finally break up with the departure of Sweden?
q-wikinger-nordeuropa-52#explanation: With the election of Gustav Vasa as king of Sweden in 1523 the union of the three realms came to an end.
